one_liner: C89 zero-allocation JSON tokenizer; beat nlohmann/json on 8 of 14 benchmark files but trails RapidJSON.
what_it_does: jsmn splits a JSON text into a flat, preorder array of tokens (object, array, string, primitive). Each token holds only start/end byte offsets into your buffer and a direct-child count: there is no DOM, no number conversion, no string unescaping and no JSON writer, so you walk the array yourself and call strtol/strtod or compare bytes where needed. The whole API is two C functions, jsmn_init and jsmn_parse, which write into a jsmntok_t array you supply. Pass NULL to get the token count; JSMN_ERROR_PART and JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM let you resume after more input or more tokens arrive.
how_it_is_fast: It does much less work than a DOM parser: one byte-at-a-time pass through a switch-based state machine that records offsets only, with no heap allocation, copying, number or escape decoding, UTF-8 validation or SIMD. A `toksuper` index tracks the enclosing container. In the default build a closing bracket finds its parent by scanning the token array backwards, which is quadratic on containers with many container children. -DJSMN_PARENT_LINKS stores a parent index in each token (4 more bytes), so that walk is bounded by nesting depth.
when_to_use: Microcontrollers (the README says it is tested on AVR and ARM) or builds with no heap and no libc, where one C89 header and a fixed stack array of 16-byte tokens (20 bytes with parent links) is all you can afford.
Small, known-schema messages such as config files or API responses where you extract a few fields and convert only those. The author's page reports good results on objects of about 4 KB.
Input that arrives in chunks over UART or a socket: call jsmn_parse again as bytes arrive until it stops returning JSMN_ERROR_PART, without building a tree.

A C or C++ hot path where nlohmann/json is the bottleneck, the documents are flat or shallow, and most values need no conversion. In the paper jsmn ran numbers.json at 0.65 vs 0.06 GB/s and github_events at 0.52 vs 0.09 GB/s.
when_not_to_use: Untrusted input that must be validated. Even with JSMN_STRICT it accepts missing commas (#217) and stray leading or trailing ':' or ',' (#247). The paper reports that it accepts [0e+]. It does not reject raw control characters in strings or check UTF-8.

Large nested documents in the default build. canada.json (GeoJSON coordinate arrays) tokenized at 0.01 GB/s, and issue #36 reports a 9 MB nested file taking about 6 s until JSMN_PARENT_LINKS was defined.

Server or desktop throughput. In the same table RapidJSON insitu, which builds a full DOM, is faster on 13 of 14 files (about 5x geomean). cJSON is faster on 11 of 14, and gason and sajson are faster on all 14.
Anything that needs lookup by key, DOM mutation, serialization, or decoded numbers and strings. You have to write that layer yourself.

Documents over 2 GB, because offsets are int and issue #44 shows negative end offsets on overflow. Also projects that need a maintainer: the last commit was 2021-10-14, with 100 open issues and 42 open PRs.

integration.form: header-only: a single jsmn.h. Define JSMN_HEADER in every .c file but one, or JSMN_STATIC to make the symbols static.
integration.dependencies: none. It includes only <stddef.h> and calls no libc functions.
integration.min_toolchain: Any C89 (ANSI C) compiler. It is usable from C++ through its extern "C" guard.
integration.platforms: Any. It is plain portable C with no SIMD. The README says it is tested on x86/amd64, ARM and AVR, and library.json declares platforms "*" (PlatformIO).
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. In the source there is no global or static mutable state: all state lives in the caller's jsmn_parser and token array. Separate parser and token pairs can run concurrently, but one parser must not be shared between threads.

gotchas: JSMN_PARENT_LINKS changes the jsmntok_t layout. Every translation unit must be built with the same setting or you get memory corruption (#70). Without it, large nested inputs are quadratic.

Non-strict mode is the default. It accepts unquoted primitives, primitives as keys, and even arrays or objects as keys. That input can give a key a child count that breaks key/value pairing (#193), and the bundled jsondump example reads out of bounds on such trees (#125, #249). Bounds-check any token walk.

`size` counts direct children only (keys, for objects), and there is no next-sibling link, so skipping a nested value means walking its whole subtree. String tokens exclude the quotes but keep escapes raw. Primitives are untyped: you tell them apart by their first byte.

Parsing stops at the first NUL byte even if len is larger. On JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM, grow the token array while keeping its contents and call jsmn_parse again with the same parser. The simdjson benchmark avoided this by allocating one 16-byte token per input byte.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick jsmn over gason, sajson or yyjson only when you need C89, no heap, no libc and a tiny footprint on a microcontroller: in the paper's Table 10, gason (0.71-1.1 GB/s) and sajson beat jsmn (0.01-0.65 GB/s) on every file, and yyjson is also ANSI C but validates to RFC 8259 and builds a full DOM with a custom allocator. If you want a real DOM without malloc, parsed into a buffer you supply, qajson4c is the closer fit.
verified_claims_summary: The simdjson paper (Langdale and Lemire, VLDB Journal 2019, Table 10) ran jsmn from a 2018 commit (18e9fe4, default build without parent links, token array sized to the input) against nlohmann/json's full DOM parse on 14 files, single-threaded on an Intel i7-6700 (Skylake) with GCC 9.1 -O3 -march=native. jsmn was faster on 8 files (e.g. numbers 0.65 vs 0.06 GB/s, twitter 0.27 vs 0.10) and slower on 6 (e.g. canada 0.01 vs 0.05), about 1.5x by geomean, while RapidJSON insitu beat it on 13 of 14; a tokenizer against a DOM parser is not like-for-like.
status_note: Abandoned: the last commit was 2021-10-14 and the last release v1.1.0 (June 2019), with 100 open issues and 42 open PRs, but it is an MIT-licensed single header with no dependencies that is easy to vendor and patch.
